IS : 3625 ( Part 4 ) - 1986 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

WARP TUBES FOR RING SPINNING AND 

DOUBLING SPINDLES 

PART 4 RECOMMENDED DIMENSIONS OR TUBES, 
TAPER 1 : 40 



(Second Revision) 



0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 4 ) (Second Revision ) was adopted by 
the Indian Standards Institution on 16 January 1986, after the draft 
finalized by the Textile Mill Accessories ( Other Than Jute ) Sectional 
Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 

0.2 The recommended dimensions of tubes included in the standard are 
based on dimensions of spindles in use in the industry. Other require- 
ments, such as type, material, finish, concentricity, water absorption and 
steam conditioning are specified in Part 1 of the standard. 

0.2.1 The other parts of this standard are: 
IS : 3625 ( Part 1 )-1983 Specific requirements ( second revision ) 

IS : 3625 ( Part 2 )-1984 Recommended dimensions for tubes, taper 
1 : 38 ( second revision ) 

IS ; 3625 ( Part 3 )-1984 Recommended dimensions for tubes, taper 
1 : 64 ( second revision ) 

0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of 
this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test or analysis, sha11.be rounded off in accor- 
dance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in 
the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified 
value in this standard. 



♦Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ). 

3 



IS : 3625 ( Part 4 ) - 1986 

1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard recommends the dimensions ( length and inside 
diameter ) of lubes with taper 1 : 40 for ring spinning and doubling 

spindles. 

1.2 It also specifies the dimensions and tolerances for the gauges for 
checking the tubes. 

2. DIMENSIONS 

2.1 The recommended dimensions are given in Table 1 read with Fig. 1 A 
and Fig. IB. 

3. DIMENSIONS FOR GAUGES 

3.1 The dimensions and tolerances of gauges for tubes of types A and B 
are given in Table 2 read with Fig. 2A and Fig. 2B. Alternate gauge 
design suitable for both type A open-top and type B rolled-in top tubes 
is shown in Fig. 3.
